trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum, earned by unlocking the other 54 trophies in a single playthrough of roughly 200 hours. Two disciplines protect the whole run. First, saves: there is no mission replay, so keep a manual save at the start and end of every chapter, as the roadmap sources advise, rotating the remaining slots during cleanup. Second, cheats: every source agrees that using a cheat disables trophies and saving, so keep your trophy save completely cheat-free. Work the five roadmap stages in order, story first and the 100 percent checklist second, and the platinum lands with the last trophy.

steps.t: Keep a manual save at the start and end of every chapter; there is no mission replay.
Never use cheats on this save; they disable trophies and saving.
Earn the other 54 trophies and the platinum unlocks automatically.

trophies.tip: Chapter saves plus a cheat-free file are the entire insurance policy for a 200-hour platinum.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The very first story trophy: simply play through the opening mission, Gone Fishing, which the game puts in front of you before the map opens up. There are no optional objectives and no way to skip past it, so treat the mission as a tutorial for driving, shooting and the partner system, and experiment freely. If you are replaying for a clean file, this pops within the first stretch of the game, long before any collectible or activity work becomes available.

steps.t: Start a new game and follow the opening prompts into Gone Fishing.
Play the mission to its end, learning the basic controls as you go.
Finish the final objective and the trophy unlocks during the wrap-up.

trophies.tip: Spend the mission learning how your partner behaves; several later trophies depend on working together.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 1 of the main story. Just keep following the story markers after the opening mission and complete every mission the chapter gives you; chapter progress is linear, so there is nothing optional hiding inside it. Use this stretch to build the habit that carries the whole platinum: after each mission, glance at the map for newly unlocked activities and strangers, because several later trophies quietly unlock their starting points during the early chapters.

steps.t: Continue the main story after Gone Fishing and clear each Chapter 1 mission.
Watch the map after every mission for new activity and stranger icons.
Complete the chapter finale and the trophy unlocks as Chapter 2 begins.

trophies.tip: Do side content as it appears rather than saving it all; the endgame grind is much shorter that way.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 2 of the main story. Keep pushing the story markers and the trophy lands when the chapter closes; the chapter structure means there is no branching path that could skip it. By now the game has usually introduced earning and spending money, so start keeping a healthy cash buffer instead of spending everything on vehicles: the money trophies later in the list are far easier when you have been banking income from the second chapter onwards.

steps.t: Play through every Chapter 2 story mission in order.
Keep a cash reserve instead of spending everything you earn.
Finish the chapter finale and the trophy unlocks as Chapter 3 begins.

trophies.tip: Money habits formed in Chapter 2 decide how painful the laundering and spending trophies feel later.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 3 of the main story. Continue following the campaign and complete the chapter's closing mission; like every chapter trophy it cannot be skipped or missed. The middle chapters are a good moment to start the repeatable counters in this guide, such as stunts and challenges, because you now have the vehicles, weapons and map access those grinds need, and chipping away at them between story missions stops them feeling like a wall at the end.

steps.t: Clear each Chapter 3 story mission as it appears on the map.
Between missions, start chipping at stunts and challenges with the counter.
Complete the chapter finale and the trophy unlocks as Chapter 4 begins.

trophies.tip: Ten stunts or challenges between story missions adds up to a finished grind before the finale.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 4 of the main story, the last full chapter before the finale. Play the chapter through to its closing mission and the trophy is yours. Because the endgame is close, this is the right time to check your stranger strands and character mission chains: their final missions form a whole family of trophies on this list, and starting them now, while story momentum is high, is far more comfortable than hunting for their first markers after the credits.

steps.t: Play through every Chapter 4 story mission in order.
Check the map for stranger and character mission chains you have not started.
Finish the chapter finale and the trophy unlocks as the endgame opens.

trophies.tip: Start every character's mission chain before the final mission so their finales are ready when you are.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold for finishing the final story mission. Timing matters here even though the trophy itself cannot be missed: before you start the finale, make a separate manual save, because a final mission is by definition the point of no return for anything tied to the story's last stretch, and a spare save is cheap insurance. Go in stocked with armour, snacks and your best weapons, complete the mission, and let the credits roll; afterwards the open world remains available for the 100 percent push and every cleanup trophy on the list.

steps.t: Before starting the finale, save manually in a separate slot as insurance.
Stock up on armour and supplies, then play the final mission to the end.
Watch the credits and the trophy unlocks as the story concludes.

trophies.tip: The separate pre-finale save is the single cheapest safety net in the whole platinum run.
trophies.riskReason: The final mission is the story's point of no return and there is no mission replay, so keep a separate manual save before you start it.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the named story mission Breakfast Run. Story missions appear in a fixed order as you progress the campaign, so if the marker is not on your map yet, the answer is simply more story progress rather than a hidden trigger. Play the mission through to its final objective; there are no optional side conditions attached to the trophy itself, and mission replay or chapter flow will always bring you back to it on a normal playthrough.

steps.t: Progress the main story until the Breakfast Run marker appears.
Start the mission and follow its objectives in order.
Complete the final objective and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Named-mission trophies are never missable while you keep one continuous story save.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist-style missions usually reward a minute of preparation, so before you trigger it, top up armour, ammunition and health items, and bring a reliable getaway-grade vehicle if the setup lets you choose one. The trophy only cares about completion, not about medals, time or loot totals, so play it safe, use cover, and let your partner draw fire when the escape gets loud.

steps.t: Progress the story until The Cartel Heist becomes available.
Restock armour, ammo and health before starting it.
Complete the heist and its escape to unlock the trophy.

trophies.tip: Completion is all that counts; a slow, careful heist earns the same trophy as a flawless one.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the story mission Child's Play. Like every named-mission trophy on this list it arrives through normal campaign progress: keep clearing story markers and the mission will be offered to you. There are no extra conditions beyond finishing it, so if you are partway through the story and have not seen it, simply keep playing; if you have finished the story, check that no earlier mission in the chain is still sitting unfinished on the map.

steps.t: Progress the main story until Child's Play is offered.
Play the mission through its objectives in order.
Finish the closing objective and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: If a named mission seems missing, an earlier unfinished mission in the chain is almost always the reason.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the story mission Headliners. It unlocks through ordinary campaign progression, so keep working the story markers and it will come to you. The trophy is tied to completion only, which means you can take the mission at whatever pace suits the gear you have; if a firefight inside it feels rough, falling back, healing and re-engaging costs you nothing but a little time.

steps.t: Progress the main story until the Headliners marker appears.
Start the mission and work through its objectives.
Complete the final objective and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: There is no medal or timer attached; patience inside hard missions is free.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the story mission VCIA Takedown. VCIA is the airport, so expect vehicles, open ground and long sightlines; bring a scoped weapon and a fast car for the approach if the setup allows free preparation. As with the other named-mission trophies, completion is the only condition: follow the objectives, finish the takedown, and the trophy unlocks as the mission wraps up. It cannot be missed on a continuous story save.

steps.t: Progress the story until VCIA Takedown becomes available.
Prepare a fast vehicle and a scoped weapon if the setup allows.
Complete the takedown and the trophy unlocks at mission end.

trophies.tip: Airport missions punish standing in the open; move between cover and vehicles.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the story mission Operation Savage Glory. An operation-style mission usually means several combat phases in a row, so enter it fully stocked and treat checkpoints as moments to breathe and re-arm from fallen enemies. The trophy needs only completion, and the mission arrives through normal story progression, so there is nothing to hunt for and nothing that can be permanently missed on your main save.

steps.t: Progress the story until Operation Savage Glory is offered.
Enter fully stocked and loot ammo between combat phases.
Finish the final phase and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Long missions are won at checkpoints: heal and re-arm every time the game gives you a pause.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The hardest trophy on the list and the real platinum gate: finish the 100 percent checklist, which appears under Progress, then Stats, then 100 percent Completion after the story, although everything you do earlier already counts. The checklist is far more forgiving than its name, closer to 60 percent of everything in the game: required in full are all robberies including the 8 bank vaults and 39 gang operations, underwater discoveries, every shooting range gold, all drone races and Bret's 15 Target Decks, while the rest is partial, including 200 of 277 vehicle scans, 100 of 255 animals studied, 15 of 18 meditations, 70 of 80 challenges and 300 stunts. Nothing on it is missable.

steps.t: Finish the story, then open Progress, Stats, 100 percent Completion and work category by category.
Clear the fully-required parts first: robberies, ranges, drone races, underwater discoveries and Bret's decks.
Top up the partial targets, 200 vehicles, 100 animals, 70 challenges, 300 stunts, until the checklist reads 100 percent.

trophies.tip: When the percentage stalls, read the checklist itself, not your memory; it names exactly what is short.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete any 250 of the 397 stunts: 130 stunt jumps, 202 under-bridge flights, 40 knife flights and 25 base jumps. Sources agree the under-bridge flights accumulate quickest; track the total under Progress, Activities, Stunts. One warning: the 100 percent checklist asks for 300, so when this pops at 250, keep going a little longer for A Long Road.

steps.t: Open Progress, Activities, Stunts and pick the stunt families that suit you.
Farm the under-bridge flights, the quickest category, whenever you fly.
Reach 250 for the trophy, then push on toward 300 for the checklist.

trophies.tip: Mix the four stunt families freely; the trophy counts the total, not any single category.
trophies.riskReason: Sources print two stunt targets side by side: 250 for this trophy and 300 for the 100 percent checklist.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once. The tracker's own list, as the guide sites report it, is fishing, hunting, golf, a shooting range, pool, basketball, an arcade or video game, a race and a stunt. Progress, then Activities shows which types you have already touched, so the method is a menu sweep: check the list, sample whatever is missing, and log each new type on the counter. Most types arrive naturally through the story and other trophies, which makes this a five-minute cleanup rather than a project, as long as you check the menu before declaring it forgotten.

steps.t: Open Progress, Activities and note which of the 9 types are still untouched.
Sample each missing type once, anywhere it is offered.
Reach all 9 types and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: The Activities menu is the checklist; trust it over your memory of what you tried.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold medals in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, spread across 12 ranges according to the two lists that count them. Ranges reward pattern learning over reflexes: take one calm scoring run to learn each challenge's target order, then chase the gold while the sequence is fresh, because retries are instant. Range work also raises your Focus level, which quietly helps Gunslinger later. Work range by range and log every gold on the counter, so the last few challenges are easy to find at cleanup instead of being one anonymous total.

steps.t: Run each range challenge once to learn its target pattern.
Replay immediately and take the gold while the pattern is fresh.
Log each gold and clear all 42 challenges across the 12 ranges.

trophies.tip: Learn first, score second: two calm runs per challenge beat ten frustrated ones.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every one of the 14 locations. The full drone calendar is bigger than the trophy: there are 42 drone races or time trials across those 14 locations, and the 100 percent checklist wants all 42, so the efficient play is to finish each location completely while you are there instead of taking one win and leaving. For the trophy itself, one win per location is enough. Learn each course with a first run, win it with the second, and log the location before you travel on.

steps.t: At each Top Fun location, learn the course with a first run.
Win a race there, then finish the location's remaining races for the checklist.
Log the location and repeat at all 14 locations.

trophies.tip: Clear each location fully in one visit; returning for leftover races is the slow way.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races; the word different does the heavy lifting, so winning the same easy race twenty times will not move this trophy at all. Tour the map's race markers, win each one once, and log every distinct win on the counter. If a particular race resists you, tune or swap your vehicle for its class rather than grinding the same start line, and remember that a win banked early counts forever, so there is never a reason to leave a race half-finished once you are leading it.

steps.t: Open the map and work through the race markers one by one.
Win each distinct race once and log it on the counter.
Reach 20 different race wins and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Change the car, not the plan: most stubborn races fall to a better-matched vehicle.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in his fishing challenge. Cal enters your game early: after you meet him in the Chapter 1 mission Feng Shui, he texts you and marks his fishing spot with a purple icon. Play through his fishing quests and take him on in the challenge itself. Fishing challenges reward steadiness, so protect every modest catch instead of gambling on one hero fish, and run the challenge straight back while your timing is warm if he takes the first round. Because his invitation arrives by text, this is an easy trophy to forget; the counter in the Next up panel will remind you it exists.

steps.t: Meet Cal in Chapter 1 and answer his text to open the fishing spot.
Play his fishing quests to learn how the challenge scores.
Beat Cal in the challenge itself and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Steady catches beat hero fish; consistency is the whole fishing game.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete any one arcade game from start to finish. There are four video games to choose from: three of them are on the TV at home, and the fourth sits on arcade cabinets around Leonida. Pick whichever suits you and actually reach its end rather than quitting at a game over. It is one of the cheapest trophies on the list and doubles as one of the nine activity types for Master of None, so an evening on the home TV can quietly bank both at once.

steps.t: Choose one of the four video games, at home on the TV or at a cabinet.
Play it through to its end without quitting.
Finish the game and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: The home TV holds three of the four games; the shortest one is the whole job.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's quest line. Andy's quests are Lucia-only and begin in Chapter 3, when he texts her an address in Belville; there are five quests in order, and the last of them awards the trophy. Because the chain belongs to one character, it will not advance while you play as Jason, so pick it up when you are in Lucia's shoes. One source reports story-progress windows on chains like this while another says every trophy quest giver is still there after the story; start the chain when it appears and you never have to care which is right.

steps.t: As Lucia, answer Andy's Chapter 3 text and go to the Belville address.
Complete his five quests in order whenever you play as Lucia.
Finish the final quest and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Lucia-only means Lucia: switch characters before you go looking for his markers.
trophies.riskReason: One source reports story-progress windows on these character chains, while another says every trophy quest giver returns after the story; start the chain as soon as it appears to stay safe.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Kenton's chain. Kenton hires you in Chapter 1, under a green KR icon in Key Lento, to recover treasure from 7 shipwrecks: dive at the purple chest markers and use the metal detector to dig the treasure up, tracking progress under Progress, Collections, Kenton's Treasures. Do not panic when he disappears after Chapter 1; the sources are explicit that he texts Jason again later, so the chain can be finished then. He is the standing example that a quiet quest giver is not a lost trophy.

steps.t: Take Kenton's Chapter 1 job in Key Lento and dive the purple chest markers at the shipwrecks.
Dig up the treasure at all 7 shipwrecks with the metal detector.
When he texts again later, finish his final mission and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Kenton vanishing after Chapter 1 is scripted, not a bug; he comes back by text.
trophies.riskReason: One source reports story-progress windows on these character chains, while another says every trophy quest giver returns after the story; start the chain as soon as it appears to stay safe.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Billy's chain. Billy's five jobs start at the Thrillbilly Mudclub in Kelly County after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, and the fifth job, Hometown Heroes, awards the trophy. The jobs stay available after the story, which makes Billy one of the safer chains on the list, but there is no reason to stockpile them: clear each job as it appears and the finale arrives on schedule. Note for your Strangers and Freaks counting: Billy's own line does not count toward that silver, since it has this trophy of its own.

steps.t: After Coffee Break in Chapter 2, start Billy's jobs at the Thrillbilly Mudclub.
Complete his five jobs in order as they unlock.
Finish Hometown Heroes and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Billy waits for you after the story, but finishing him early keeps the cleanup list short.
trophies.riskReason: One source reports story-progress windows on these character chains, while another says every trophy quest giver returns after the story; start the chain as soon as it appears to stay safe.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 qualifying mission strands for strangers across Leonida. The trap in this silver is the word qualifying: not every stranger line counts. The fullest named list says Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete count, while the lines belonging to Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, Andy, Billy and Eddie do not, because those characters carry trophies of their own. Yago's strand even contains a timed Chapter 3 race, so do it the moment it appears. The only fully reliable referee is the trophy's own progress counter in your trophy list, so check it after every finished strand and log only the strands that moved it.

steps.t: Start stranger strands as their markers appear across the state.
After each finished strand, check the trophy progress counter actually moved.
Log only qualifying strands and reach 8 to unlock the trophy.

trophies.tip: The progress counter is the referee; a finished strand that did not move it never counted.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Randy's chain, which is a delivery list: Randy's Wish List asks you to deliver 16 cars, and the chain runs from Chapter 3. Treat each wanted car as a small contract: find the model, take it cleanly, and deliver it rather than a damaged substitute, and work the list down steadily instead of hunting all 16 in one session. Randy's deliveries also count among the optional missions the 100 percent checklist wants, so the chain pays you twice. As with the other character lines, start it when it appears rather than leaving it to a crowded cleanup.

steps.t: Pick up Randy's Wish List from Chapter 3 and note the 16 cars.
Find and deliver each wanted car in good condition.
Deliver the final car, complete his last mission, and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Deliver cars clean; a wrecked wishlist car is a wasted trip across the map.
trophies.riskReason: One source reports story-progress windows on these character chains, while another says every trophy quest giver returns after the story; start the chain as soon as it appears to stay safe.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Tyrone's chain. Tyrone's line is Jason-only and runs from Chapter 3, ending with the destruction of the labs and his last quest, so it advances only while you play as Jason. Because Tyrone has this trophy of his own, his strand does not count toward the Strangers and Freaks silver; keep the two ledgers separate in your head and in this tracker. Start the chain when it appears, work it whenever you are in Jason's shoes, and the finale closes both the story and the trophy.

steps.t: As Jason, start Tyrone's chain from Chapter 3.
Work his quests in order, including the lab jobs, as Jason.
Finish his final quest and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Jason-only, like Andy is Lucia-only: check whose shoes you are in before travelling.
trophies.riskReason: One source reports story-progress windows on these character chains, while another says every trophy quest giver returns after the story; start the chain as soon as it appears to stay safe.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida: 18 meditations over 10 locations. Start with the one that can hurt you: in Chapter 1, after Down to Earth, Lucia walks onto the balcony at Jason's house and invites you to meditate — follow her and accept. It disappears when Chapter 1 ends, and sources have not confirmed whether the trophy requires it, so treat it as required. Every outdoor spot counts twice, once per character; both are playable after Chapter 2's Coffee Break. Track progress under Progress, Collections, Exploration, Meditations. The last spot, on Mount Kalaga's summit, appears only once the rest are done. The checklist needs 15 of 18; the trophy needs all 18.

steps.t: In Chapter 1, after Down to Earth, follow Lucia to the balcony at Jason's house and accept the meditation.
From Chapter 2 on, meditate at each outdoor spot with both Jason and Lucia, counting 2 per spot.
Finish with the Ascent spot on Mount Kalaga and reach 18 of 18.

trophies.tip: The balcony meditation is free in Chapter 1 and priceless later; never leave the chapter without it.
trophies.riskReason: The first meditation, on the balcony at Jason's house with Lucia in Chapter 1, disappears when the chapter ends, and sources have not confirmed whether the trophy requires it; both characters count toward the 18.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret Vogel's hunting questline is Jason-only and opens after Chapter 2; it runs through his Target Decks, 15 hunting objectives that the 100 percent checklist also wants in full. For clean kills, the hunting sources advise a head or heart shot so the carcass stays pristine. One honest unknown: which unique animal this trophy wants is still unconfirmed by the guide sites, so work Bret's decks in order and let the questline itself present the animal, rather than hunting a rumoured species on your own.

steps.t: As Jason, start Bret's hunting quests after Chapter 2.
Work the Target Deck hunts in order, taking clean head or heart shots.
Complete the unique-animal hunt Bret sets you and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Pristine carcasses come from one clean shot; spray and pray ruins hunts.
trophies.riskReason: The hunt itself is confirmed, but which unique animal Bret sends you after is still unconfirmed by the guide sites.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets. There are 18 sets in the game, and the 100 percent checklist eventually asks for 15 of them, so this silver is an early down payment on a longer road: think in sets, not in single cards. Pick the sets you are closest to finishing, sweep their remaining cards region by region, and log each completed set on the counter. If you are going for the platinum anyway, there is no wasted motion here; every set you finish now is one the checklist will not ask you to revisit later.

steps.t: Check which card sets are closest to complete.
Sweep the missing cards of those sets region by region.
Complete 3 full sets for the trophy, and keep going toward 15 for the checklist.

trophies.tip: Nearest sets first: three finished sets now, fifteen eventually, all on the same road.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK app at 100 locations. The 100 locations are a mix of four kinds of points of interest, Landmarks, Curiosities, Sculptures and No Flusher tags, so variety is built into the requirement: a sweep of only one kind cannot finish it. The habit that earns this quietly is to scan whenever you arrive somewhere new, before you do anything else there. The counter here tracks the total, and since the 100 percent checklist asks for exactly the same 100 scans, every scan you log is final, with no second, larger target hiding behind this one.

steps.t: Scan with WAiNK whenever you arrive somewhere new and log it.
Mix the four kinds of spots, landmarks, curiosities, sculptures and tags.
Reach 100 scanned locations and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Scan on arrival, every time; this trophy is a habit, not a hunt.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 Challenges. The challenge pool holds 80 challenges, listed under Progress, then Challenges, and they complete largely on their own as you play, which is why this bronze usually arrives without a dedicated grind. The number to hold in your head is the pair, not the single figure: the trophy wants 50, while the 100 percent checklist wants 70 of the 80, deliberately allowing you to skip the ten hardest. Work the easy completions first, log them on the counter, and if you are bound for the platinum, simply keep going past 50 until 70 are done.

steps.t: Open Progress, Challenges and finish the challenges closest to completion.
Log each finished challenge on the counter.
Reach 50 for the trophy, then 70 of 80 for the 100 percent checklist.

trophies.tip: Skip the ten hardest challenges without guilt; the checklist is designed to let you.
trophies.riskReason: Sources print two challenge targets side by side: 50 for this trophy and 70 of 80 for the 100 percent checklist.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you and escape the heat. The reliable setup uses the robbery game itself: a bank vault job hands you 4 stars the moment it turns loud, so escaping a vault with your partner can earn this trophy and progress Maximum Withdrawal in the same minute. For the escape, the sources name a favourite: the train tunnel north of Ambrosia in Kelly County, where road units struggle to follow and the helicopter loses sight of you. Remember the trophy completes only once you have left the red heat zone entirely, not merely broken the search circle.

steps.t: Raise a 4-star wanted level with your partner present, ideally from a bank vault job.
Head for the train tunnel north of Ambrosia and break line of sight along the tracks.
Leave the red heat zone completely and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: The vault gives you the stars and the tunnel takes them away; pair the two trophies.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level between them. Plan the geography first: the three jewelry stores in the north of Vice City sit close together, which keeps the driving short and the heat alive. Rob the first, drive straight to the second while the stars are still on you, then the third; if you hide and cool down at any point, the chain is broken. One patience note from the sources: the trophy is delayed and can take about 30 seconds to appear after you leave the third shop, so give it that moment before robbing a fourth in frustration.

steps.t: Bring your partner to the close-together jewelry stores in north Vice City.
Rob the first shop and drive to the second without letting the wanted level drop.
Rob the second and third, then wait up to 30 seconds for the delayed trophy.

trophies.tip: Judge the chain after 30 seconds, not at the third door; this trophy pops late.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Discovery here means scanning: a WAiNK scan of a vehicle counts as discovering it, with no need to drive or own it, so the fastest method is scanning traffic as you travel, especially near busy roads where models rotate quickly. Build the habit from Chapter 1, when the app unlocks, and the trophy tends to complete itself during the story. Keep the bigger number in mind for later: the 100 percent checklist wants 200 of the 277 base models scanned, so every scan you log now is doing double duty.

steps.t: Unlock the WAiNK app in Chapter 1 and scan every unfamiliar vehicle you pass.
Scan traffic near busy roads where new models rotate in quickly.
Reach 100 discovered vehicles, then keep scanning toward 200 for the checklist.

trophies.tip: You never need to drive them; a scan is a discovery, so scan everything that moves.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-motion aim, triggered by pressing both sticks while aiming, and the setup matters more than the shooting. Fill your Focus first, with food, drink or a shower at home, carry adrenaline to stretch the activation, and choose the right crowd: gang members at an illegal operation, because the sources report that soldiers, police and civilians do not appear to count. Line the group up, trigger Focus with an assault rifle in hand, and move target to target without breaking rhythm.

steps.t: Fill your Focus meter and carry adrenaline before the attempt.
Find at least five gang members together, for example at an illegal operation.
Activate Combat Focus and take down all 5 enemies in the single activation.

trophies.tip: Gang members count and uniforms apparently do not; choose the crowd before the ability.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA by stealing a passenger jet. Not any plane counts: the aircraft must be a large airliner docked at a boarding bridge, and the sources name gates E3 and E4 as the reliable spots. Timing note: do this during relaxed free-roam play and save first, because the police response is fast and the trophy itself is delayed; it pops only once you are about 1 kilometre away from the airport, so do not circle back early wondering why nothing happened. Get in, back out toward the runway, take off, and fly the kilometre.

steps.t: Save first, then reach a passenger jet docked at a boarding bridge, gates E3 or E4.
Get into the cockpit, back out to the runway and take off.
Fly about 1 kilometre from VCIA and the delayed trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: The kilometre is part of the requirement; fly away first, celebrate second.
trophies.riskReason: It needs a passenger jet docked at a boarding bridge and a clean 1 kilometre flight out; do it during relaxed free roam and save first, before late-story cleanup crowds your list.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The joke description points at the Rhino, the military tank: steal one and use it in combat. Guide sites place the tanks at Mile Zero Air Station on Goose Key, parked on the south side of the base. Save before you go in, because a military base answers theft with force: get into a Rhino, drive it out of trouble or straight into it, and take out enemies from inside the armour until the trophy pops. The counter-free, one-and-done nature of it makes this a good trophy to bank in a single deliberate trip rather than by accident.

steps.t: Save manually, then head to Mile Zero Air Station on Goose Key.
Reach a Rhino tank on the south side of the base and get inside.
Take out enemies from inside the tank until the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Save first and commit: hesitation inside a military base is what gets you killed, not the tank.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store cleanly, start to finish, with nobody spotting you. The tool that makes it possible is the Snap Gun, which reaches you through Yasmani's Chapter 3 jewelry jobs: use it on a store's locked back door, because kicking the door in sets off the alarm and ends the attempt. Inside the back room, find the note carrying the safe code, open the safe, take what is there and leave the way you came. If anyone spots you at any point, reload and run it again; the trophy rewards one perfect, quiet pass, not a fast one.

steps.t: Finish Yasmani's Chapter 3 jewelry jobs to receive the Snap Gun.
Enter a jewelry store through its back door with the Snap Gun, never by force.
Take the safe code from the back room, empty the safe and leave unseen.

trophies.tip: Slow is smooth here: one unseen pass beats five loud ones, and a reload costs nothing.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: A silver for robbing 5 of the game's 8 bank vaults and escaping each time. Vaults are not open from the start: they unlock through the optional Chapter 4 mission That's Where The Money Is, after which you follow a security van to a bank and slip into the vault while it stands open. Bring your partner, because the bags are too much to carry alone, and expect an instant 4-star wanted level the moment the job turns loud, so have a fast bike staged for the escape. That guaranteed 4-star heat is also why this trophy pairs naturally with Hot Together: escape a vault with your partner and both can pop from the same job.

steps.t: Complete the optional Chapter 4 mission that unlocks bank vaults.
Follow a security van in, enter the open vault with your partner and fill the bags.
Escape the 4-star heat; repeat at 5 different vaults and log each on the counter.

trophies.tip: Stage the escape bike before you enter; the vault gives you money and stars in equal measure.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and get away. Watch for armored trucks on your travels, block or disable the truck, deal with its guards, take the money and then focus entirely on the escape, because the trophy is only earned once you are clear. Guide sites note that a bank vault job can also satisfy this if you get away from one, so if armored trucks prove shy on your save, the vault work you are doing anyway for Maximum Withdrawal may hand you this trophy on the side.

steps.t: Spot an armored truck and stop it somewhere you can work quickly.
Take the money from the truck and deal with its guards.
Escape the wanted level completely and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Plan the escape before the robbery; the truck is the easy part, the heat is the trophy.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida, which in practice means clearing the fog from the entire map. Ground travel unfogs slowly, so the method the guide sites agree on is air travel: take a plane and sweep the dark patches systematically, county by county, until no fog remains. Do this late in your run, when most of the map is already clear from story and cleanup travel, and treat whatever dark corners survive as a checklist of their own. It pairs well with the final meditation and any last collectibles, since all of them send you to the state's edges.

steps.t: Check the map late in your run and note which areas are still fogged.
Take a plane and sweep the dark patches county by county.
Clear the last fogged areas and the trophy unlocks at full coverage.

trophies.tip: Altitude is the shortcut: one methodical flight clears what weeks of driving would miss.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. There are 39 operations in total and the 100 percent checklist eventually wants all of them, but this trophy only needs breadth: one confirmed robbery per gang, tracked on the counter here. When you hit an operation, note which gang it belonged to before you move on, because nine similar raids blur together quickly. The gang operations are also the recommended hunting ground for Gunslinger, since their guards are exactly the enemy type Combat Focus works best against.

steps.t: Find an illegal operation and check which gang runs it.
Rob it and log that gang on the counter before moving on.
Cover all 9 gangs, one operation each, and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Log the gang, not just the robbery; breadth across 9 gangs is the whole requirement.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Timing note first: this is one of the five trophies whose exact trigger the guide sites still list as unconfirmed, so do not leave it for the very end of your run. Try it early, while Ocean Beach is still the centre of your routine in the opening chapters: go to the beachfront, find where drinks are served with the ocean in view, and have the cocktail there. If it does not pop on a first attempt, retry it at a different beachfront spot or time of day as you pass through the area during the story, rather than forcing it in one sitting; an unconfirmed trigger rewards early, repeated, low-cost attempts.

steps.t: Timing: attempt this early, from your first free time on Ocean Beach onward.
Find a beachfront spot serving drinks with a view of the ocean and order a cocktail.
If it does not pop, retry at another Ocean Beach spot as you pass through during the story.

trophies.tip: Early and often beats late and desperate: unconfirmed triggers should be attempted while they cost nothing.
trophies.riskReason: Its exact trigger is still unconfirmed and it belongs to Ocean Beach, the centre of your early-game routine; attempt it early and often instead of leaving an unconfirmed trigger for the end.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. This is another of the five trophies the guide sites still mark unconfirmed, but the shared reading of the description is consistent: get into a car inside a vehicle showroom and drive it out through the showroom window rather than any door. Pick a showroom with a car you can reach, get in, line up the glass, and commit to the exit. Because the trigger is unconfirmed, treat a non-pop as information, not failure: try a different showroom or a faster run at the window before you conclude anything.

steps.t: Enter a vehicle showroom and get into one of the display cars.
Line the car up with the showroom window, not a doorway.
Drive out through the glass in one committed run.

trophies.tip: The window is the point of the trophy; a polite exit through the door earns nothing.
trophies.riskReason: One of the five trophies guide sites still list as unconfirmed; the showroom-window reading is shared but not yet proven.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: The bowling alley in the description is the Kingpin Bowling gang operation in Port Gellhorn, run under the Kolt & Associates name. Guide sites describe the job the same way: rob the operation, take all 3 key valuables from the alley, and then lose the police. Treat it as a small heist with a clean getaway rather than a game of bowling: clear the valuables first, keep the escape vehicle close, and do not consider the trophy earned until the heat is fully gone, because the escape is part of the requirement.

steps.t: Go to the Kingpin Bowling operation in Port Gellhorn.
Take all 3 key valuables from the bowling alley.
Lose the police completely and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Valuables first, getaway second: the trophy completes only once the heat is gone.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Behind the cryptic description sits a stat grind: maximise the Strength stat for both Jason and Lucia. The efficient route is the gym, together: buy a gym membership and train with your partner present, because the partner trains alongside you and gains at the same time, doubling the value of every session. Work it into your routine early, a few sessions whenever you pass a gym, and the two Strength bars climb steadily instead of becoming an endgame wall. It is also one of the few trophies that quietly rewards playing as both characters rather than favouring one.

steps.t: Buy a gym membership and bring your partner to train with you.
Train Strength with both characters present so both gain together.
Max out Strength for Jason and Lucia and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Always train as a pair; solo sessions take twice as long for the same trophy.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: This guide's one missable-flagged trophy, and the flag is about permanence: the trophy tracks 500 actions that change your Criminal Profile, and profile consequences cannot be unwound on the same save. Robberies, fights and other criminal choices feed the counter as you play, so for most players it fills naturally long before the endgame. The trap to avoid is the Irredeemable profile state, which multiple guide sites stress is permanent and makes the police permanently more aggressive; play boldly, but do not let a rampage push your profile into a state you cannot walk back while you are still filling this counter.

steps.t: Play criminal content freely; robberies and fights feed the 500-action counter.
Check your Criminal Profile progress in the trophy tracker as it climbs.
Reach 500 profile-changing actions, while steering clear of the permanent Irredeemable state.

trophies.tip: Bold is fine, Irredeemable is forever: it is the one profile state no source says you can undo.
trophies.riskReason: Its 500 Criminal Profile actions come from choices you make in play, and permanent profile states such as Irredeemable cannot be undone on the same save.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: One of the five trophies whose exact trigger remains unconfirmed at the time of writing, so this guide shows you the honest state of knowledge instead of a invented recipe. The description hints at succeeding on a second attempt at something that failed the first time. The practical approach: when something in the world fails on you, a robbery gone wrong, a race lost at the line, an activity botched, go straight back and succeed at the same thing, and note whether the trophy moves. Until a source confirms the trigger, treat every failure as a free attempt at this trophy rather than wasted time.

steps.t: When an activity or job fails, return to the same one immediately.
Succeed at it on the second attempt and watch for the trophy.
If it does not pop, keep pairing failures with immediate retries as you play.

trophies.tip: Fail forward: an instant successful retry is the best current reading of this description.
trophies.riskReason: One of the five trophies guide sites still list as unconfirmed; the second-attempt reading comes only from its description.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Another of the five still-unconfirmed trophies: the description points at witnessing something strange, and the leading reading among guide sites is a weird event somewhere out in Leonida rather than a story beat. There is no confirmed location or trigger to hand you, and this guide will not invent one. What you can do is maximise exposure: explore the state's odd corners, especially at night and away from the cities, follow up anything that looks deliberately out of place, and let full-map exploration for The Goodtime State double as your search. When it pops, it will almost certainly be somewhere you wandered into, not somewhere you were sent.

steps.t: Explore remote and unusual corners of Leonida, including at night.
Investigate anything that looks deliberately out of place.
Witness the strange event and the trophy unlocks; no confirmed trigger exists yet.

trophies.tip: Wander with intent: unconfirmed event trophies reward explorers, not route-followers.
trophies.riskReason: One of the five trophies guide sites still list as unconfirmed; no location or trigger has been confirmed yet.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by: from a moving vehicle, strike a pedestrian or enemy with a melee attack as you pass them, bowling them over. The requirement is plain even though guide sites note the precise method is still being confirmed, so experiment with the variables: vehicle speed, the melee swing timing as you pass, and the type of target. A slow pass close alongside the target gives you the widest timing window. Like the other unconfirmed-method trophies, bank attempts cheaply during ordinary travel instead of staging an afternoon around it.

steps.t: Drive slowly past a target you can reach from the vehicle.
Swing your melee attack as you pass so the strike connects at speed.
Knock the target down with the drive-by hit and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Slow and close wins: a crawl-speed pass gives the melee swing time to land.
trophies.riskReason: The requirement is readable from its description, but the precise melee drive-by method is still being confirmed.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder a cumulative $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from bank and payday loan jobs, and laundering means selling them on to your fences and contacts rather than spending them raw. The total is cumulative, so every job counts, and the 100 percent checklist's robbery requirements generate marked bills in bulk along the way. Guide sites single out Yasmani as the contact who pays the most, so route your bills through the best-paying fence when you have the choice, and let the counter here track the running total in dollars.

steps.t: Run bank and payday loan jobs to collect Marked Bills.
Launder the bills through your contacts, favouring the best-paying fence.
Reach a cumulative $250,000 laundered and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Cumulative means patient: sell every batch of marked bills instead of sitting on them.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend a cumulative $100,000 across all shops. Every kind of shop counts toward the same running total, so this is a trophy your ordinary play fills on its own: weapons, ammunition, vehicles services, clothes and property-adjacent spending all push the same number. There is no reason to waste money on purpose; between restocking for heists, garages and general play, most players cross the line during the checklist phase. The counter here tracks the total in dollars so you can see how close the background grind is without changing how you play.

steps.t: Spend normally across every kind of shop as you play.
Let big legitimate purchases, like garages and gear, carry the total.
Reach a cumulative $100,000 spent and the trophy unlocks.

trophies.tip: Never buy junk for this trophy; the checklist phase spends six figures on its own.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties that are actually for sale. They are bought through the Vice City Real Estate app, which unlocks after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver, and together they cost roughly $160,000, so this trophy is a savings goal more than a task. The 4 garages the story gives you do not count toward the 8, a detail that catches players who think they already own half the list. Buy them as your income allows during the checklist phase; the space is genuinely useful, because registered vehicles each need a free garage slot.

steps.t: Unlock the Vice City Real Estate app after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver.
Save roughly $160,000 across your robbery and checklist income.
Buy all 8 purchasable garages, not counting the 4 story garages, and log each one.

trophies.tip: Buy garages before registering cars: every registered vehicle needs a free slot waiting for it.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app opens through the Chapter 2 mission Moses: take a car to Moses, choose Respray and then Register, and the vehicle is yours on the app. From Chapter 3 you can also register cars fitted with a standard tracker at a Pay 'n' Spray. Every registration needs a free garage space, so the cheap route is to register inexpensive cars into whatever slots you have, buying garages first if space runs out. Ten registrations is a small number once the system is open, and the counter here keeps track.

steps.t: Complete the Chapter 2 mission Moses to open the Scooter Bros app.
Take a car to Moses, choose Respray, then Register it to the app.
Register 10 vehicles, keeping a free garage space ready for each one.

trophies.tip: Register cheap cars: the app counts vehicles, not value, and each one needs garage space.
trophies.riskReason: No missable or timing risk reported by the sources read; it stays completable in free roam after the story.

Beebom — All GTA 6 Meditation Spots Locations
GTABase — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Achievements List

disputes.topic: How many meditations does the trophy need: 15 or 18?
disputes.a: 15 meditations complete the requirement (Beebom's completion coverage; the checklist figure in eGamers' comparison table).
disputes.b: All 18 meditations are required (PowerPyx meditation guide; GTABase's trophy figure in the same table).
disputes.call: Both numbers are real and measure different things: the trophy needs all 18, the 100 percent checklist needs 15 of 18.

disputes.topic: Is the Chapter 1 balcony meditation required for the trophy?
disputes.a: It counts toward Positive Mental Attitude and disappears after Chapter 1 (OutputLag).
disputes.b: Still pending confirmation: it is not marked as a meditation spot, and the final meditation may count double (PowerPyx).
disputes.call: Treat it as required and do it in Chapter 1. It costs two minutes; skipping it risks a replay up to Chapter 2.

disputes.topic: Do character quest chains have story-progress windows?
disputes.a: The chains behind five hidden trophies have windows tied to story progress (TechWiser, as reported by eGamers).
disputes.b: Every trophy quest giver is still there, or returns, after the story; Kenton is only temporarily unavailable (PowerPyx).
disputes.call: Start each chain when it appears, but never panic over a quiet giver: the weight of sources says they come back.

disputes.topic: How many shooting ranges are there: 12 or 2?
disputes.a: 42 gold medals across 12 ranges (GTA-Zone and GameMapa).
disputes.b: There should be two shooting ranges with 42 gold medals between them (OutputLag, hedged).
disputes.call: We go with 12 ranges and 42 golds: two independent lists agree on 12, and the rival claim hedges itself.

disputes.topic: Which stranger strands count toward the 8?
disputes.a: Kirk, Kyle, Yago and Pilot Pete count; Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, Andy, Billy and Eddie do not (GTABase).
disputes.b: Only some questlines count; check the trophy's own progress counter after each strand (OutputLag).
disputes.call: Trust the in-game progress counter after every finished strand; the named lists are still incomplete.

disputes.topic: Why do the same grinds carry two different numbers?
disputes.a: Trophy targets: 250 stunts, 20 races, 50 challenges, 3 card sets, 5 vaults (the official descriptions, compared by eGamers).
disputes.b: Checklist targets: 300 stunts, 30 races, 70 challenges, 15 card sets, 8 vaults (the 100 percent checklist figures).
disputes.call: Both are right, for different goals: trophies pop at the lower number, and only A Long Road needs the higher one.
